You may still think of a wireless carrier as a stock that holds up in a selloff. So how far has T-Mobile stock fallen in past market selloffs?
T-Mobile Stock's 54% Drop In 2011, Much Of It In One Day
T-Mobile stock recorded its steepest fall in a market shock since 2007 during the US debt ceiling crisis. From July to October 2011, the shares fell 54%, compared with an 18% decline for the S&P 500 over the same months. Market pressure alone does not fully explain the drop. The shares fell from $20.38 to $12.92 on August 2, 2011, a 37% drop in one day.
The 2008-2009 financial crisis marked the next steepest drop. T-Mobile stock fell 47% during that time, a milder decline than the 53% loss for the S&P 500. Over a longer stretch, from a peak in 2007 to a low in 2010, the stock fell 86%.
Historically, T-Mobile stock has traded through 15 market shocks since 2007. A typical event has been much milder. The stock fell 18.0% on average across these shocks, compared with 15.8% for the index. On average, the shares have dropped slightly more than the broader market.
How Long Did T-Mobile Stock Take To Recover?
The median recovery time from a low was 3.7 months, though four rebounds took more than a year. T-Mobile ultimately returned to its pre-shock high after 13 of the 14 shocks in which it fell. The stock needed 20.6 months to recover from the 2011 decline, a window that includes the one-day break in price. Following the credit crunch of summer 2007, a full recovery required 111.2 months.
Only one recovery remains unfinished. T-Mobile stock is still 43% below the high it reached before the 2025 tariff shock.
Which Of T-Mobile's Numbers Are Getting Worse?
Several underlying metrics are weakening. T-Mobile reported a slipping profit margin, slower sales growth in the latest quarter, and elevated debt compared with the broader market. The company retained 20% of its sales as operating profit over the past twelve months, down from 23% a year earlier. Sales grew 7.9% in the latest quarter from a year before, a deceleration from the 10.6% growth in the prior quarter. When the company reports on October 28, 2026, the key metric to watch will be the net number of postpaid accounts T-Mobile added in the third quarter.

iPhone Handoff is an iOS 27 feature that lets you share one number between two phones easily. Jeff Carlson/CNET
Verizon has now played its hand in supporting Apple’s new iPhone Handoff feature in iOS 27, which lets you easily switch between two iPhones using a single phone number. Just by unlocking the phone you want to use, your calls, texts, voicemails and Find My location automatically move over.
At launch, the feature is supported only by T-Mobile and Verizon in the US. Along with the rollout of the iPhone Duo, Verizon announced that it will charge $10 a month for the service, which will be supported “soon.” T-Mobile is charging $5 a month. AT&T is sitting this feature out for now.
iPhone Handoff is similar to what the Apple Watch has done with data for a few generations: taking off one watch and putting on another automatically switches all of your information, such as activity tracking, to the new one. For example, some people use one watch during the day — perhaps the rugged Apple Watch Ultra — and switch to a slimmer, older Apple Watch at night, allowing the first to charge for the morning.
But replicating that behavior to the iPhone requires coordination with cellular providers. Each phone’s eSIM needs to be configured for iPhone Handoff by a carrier, and service needs to switch cleanly on the network side.
Ironically, the Apple Watch gets left out of the iPhone Handoff transaction: Your watch remains paired with just one iPhone, communicating with it via Wi-Fi or cellular (if that’s an option). “If neither is available,” Apple writes, “calls, messages, notifications, certain health and fitness features, Siri AI or other app experiences relayed from your paired iPhone may not be available.”
In its press release about offering the iPhone 18 Pro, T-Mobile writes, “iPhone Handoff is available on any iPhone with iOS 27 via iPhone settings and ready to use from day one on the new iPhone 18 Pro lineup and iPhone Duo. T-Mobile is introducing the feature at $5/month.”
When I reached out to T-Mobile asking about the charge, a spokesperson wrote via email, “The $5/month charge reflects the added service that powers the experience on both devices.”
A Verizon representative did not have further details to share.
While iPhone Handoff appears to seamlessly switch your eSIM just by picking up the phone you want to use, it’s not yet clear what else is different with this process versus just transferring your eSIM manually using your iPhone’s settings menu.
Notably absent from Apple’s news was the other major US carrier, AT&T. I contacted a spokesperson there to learn more about the company’s plans for the feature, but it sounds like it’s not a priority.
“While we see that there could be potential in capabilities like iPhone Handoff,” the spokesperson replied, “our focus remains on delivering innovations that make life simpler and keep customers connected with confidence.” They then pointed to “existing eSIM activation and transfer options across compatible devices.”
In addition to T-Mobile and Verizon, iPhone Handoff is currently supported by Deutsche Telekom in Germany. The UK carrier EE will also support the feature later this year, according to Apple.

Jessica Uhl Appointed CFO Designate; To Succeed Peter Osvaldik as Chief Financial Officer in February 2027
Peter Osvaldik to Continue as CFO Through a Transition Period Before Assuming a Strategic Advisor Role Until His Planned July 1, 2027
BELLEVUE, Wash. — Thursday, September 3, 2026 — T-Mobile US,
Inc. (NASDAQ: TMUS) today announced that Jessica Uhl will join the company as CFO Designate and succeed Peter Osvaldik as Chief Financial Officer in February 2027, as part of the company’s long-term leadership succession planning. The
announcement follows Osvaldik’s previous one-year contract extension to support the CEO transition.
former Chief Financial Officer of Shell and most recently President of GE Vernova, will join T-Mobile as CFO Designate effective mid-September. Uhl will work alongside
current Chief Financial Officer Peter Osvaldik during an extended transition period and will succeed him as CFO in February 2027. Osvaldik will then assume a Strategic Advisor role until his planned retirement from
T-Mobile at the conclusion of his contract on July 1, 2027.
Uhl brings extensive financial and strategic
leadership experience from a 30-year career leading large-scale global businesses and prudently allocating capital. As CFO of Shell, one of the world’s largest and most complex enterprises, she oversaw
financial strategy, capital markets execution and investor relations across a business operating in more than 70 countries. She developed and led emerging businesses across Shell’s diverse portfolio, spanning infrastructure, commodity and
consumer markets.
Most recently, as President of GE Vernova, Uhl oversaw corporate development, strategy, ventures research and development, as well as
the company’s generative AI program. Her experience leading through transformation, allocating capital at scale, scaling new businesses and deploying emerging technologies, positions her to partner with
T-Mobile’s leadership team as the company advances its next era of disruption, profitable growth and innovation.
“I am thrilled to welcome Jessica to T-Mobile,” said Srini Gopalan, President and CEO of T-Mobile. “She brings deep financial and strategic acumen, capital allocation expertise and an innovative growth mindset that is a perfect fit for T-Mobile’s next
era. Jessica has a distinguished track record leading complex businesses, effectively balancing strategic investments with financial and operational discipline. After a thorough search process, I am confident Jessica is the right leader to help
shape our growth agenda as CFO, and I am grateful she and Peter will collaborate through an extended transition period to ensure continuity and a seamless succession.”
Osvaldik joined T-Mobile in 2016 and has served as Chief Financial Officer since 2020. He will continue as CFO through
February 2027, when he will assume a Strategic Advisor role until his planned retirement. The transition is designed to provide continuity across T-Mobile’s financial organization, investor and capital
markets relationships, and broader strategic priorities, while enabling a seamless transfer of leadership and institutional knowledge. Osvaldik’s tenure as CFO has been defined by disciplined financial stewardship, consistent financial
outperformance, and an unwavering commitment to T-Mobile’s mission.

added Gopalan. “Over more than a decade with the company, his financial rigor, strategic clarity and care for our mission have helped build T-Mobile into the dynamic, innovative and customer-obsessed
company it is today. The strong financial foundation Peter has solidified will help propel T-Mobile into its next chapter of growth and expansion. I am deeply grateful for Peter’s partnership and his
continued commitment to T-Mobile, from extending his contract to support my transition to CEO to helping ensure continuity as we welcome Jessica and prepare for our next chapter. We wish him the very best in
his well-earned retirement.
“T-Mobile is entering a period of extraordinary opportunity,” Gopalan
concluded. “We have a long growth runway to continue our leadership in consumer wireless by bringing America’s Best Network to more customers in small markets and rural areas and winning network seekers; accelerating our growth beyond
consumer wireless to broadband, T-Mobile for Business and new adjacencies; and further strengthening the customer differentiation that defines this company. Jessica will be a critical strategic and operational
partner as we execute with focus, scale our ambitions and create lasting value for customers, employees and shareholders.”
